title: Backend mid systemdesign job scheduler
question: Design a job scheduling system that lets other services schedule a task to run once at a specific future time, or on a recurring interval (like a cron job).
idealAnswer:
Uses persistent storage for job definitions (schedule, next run time, payload) rather than an in-memory timer list, so scheduled jobs survive a restart

Describes a polling or dispatch loop that periodically queries for jobs due to run (next_run_time <= now) rather than trying to keep a live timer per job in memory

Addresses the exactly-once-ish execution problem: when a worker picks up a due job, it needs to atomically claim it (e.g. a conditional update setting status to 'running' and a lock/lease) so a second worker or a retry of the poll doesn't also pick it up and double-execute it

Handles recurring jobs by computing and writing the next_run_time after a successful run, and handles a crashed or stuck job with a lease timeout that lets another worker reclaim it

Considers scaling the dispatch across multiple scheduler instances without duplicate execution, e.g. via the same claim mechanism, and mentions monitoring for jobs that are late or failing repeatedly
